target_customer: Teams running AI agents or LLM features in regulated industries (healthcare, finance, insurance, legal)
problem: LLM judges and human review are costly and miss agent mistakes; teams need cheap per-step checking of answers and actions.
business_model: Usage-based API and gateway, hosted or in customer cloud (pricing not found)
product_category: AI control layer using model interpretability

founders.name: Vedant Gaur
founders.background_notes: Published interpretability research at ACL and EMNLP and NeurIPS workshops per YC launch post.

technical_complexity.rationale: Reading model internals reliably across self-hosted and API models is research-heavy; the claimed 99% catch rate is self-reported.

defensibility.rationale: Probe quality and per-customer calibration could compound, but interpretability work is public and well-funded rivals exist.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Too early to tell; labs and interpretability startups already offer overlapping monitoring.

market_need_then: Enterprises deploying agents in 2026 pay for LLM judges and review; the company claims 600x lower cost than an LLM judge (self-reported).

branding.domain_note: Uses runlatent.ai (and pip package runlatent) rather than latent.com

brand_strength.rationale: Brand is brand-new; sources only coverage by Fondo.

outcome_analysis: Latent is a one-person Fall 2026 YC company with strong research credentials and bold self-reported benchmarks but no public customers or funding yet. Its main risks are competing interpretability startups, labs offering similar monitoring, and unverified performance claims.
notes: Funding none found. Competitors Goodfire and Envariant (YC W26) surfaced in 2026 coverage but without verified dates near the batch, so are not listed as dated competitors. The generic word 'latent' causes search confusion with Latent Space, latent.ai and others. Fondo article is the only independent coverage.
